findings.title: Missing double-check after acquiring write lock causes redundant work
findings.body: After acquiring entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Lock() at line 48, the code does not re-check whether entryPointAssetsCache was already populated by another goroutine that raced to the lock first (and whether cfg.Env != setting.Dev). If multiple goroutines call GetWebAssets concurrently while the cache is still nil (e.g., first requests at startup), each will block on the lock sequentially and then each will redundantly re-read the manifest file (or hit the CDN) and overwrite entryPointAssetsCache again, even though another goroutine already populated it moments earlier. This is a 'thundering herd' / wasted-work issue; the fix correctly removes the data race but does not restore the original single-computation behavior for concurrent cold-cache calls.

findings.title: No test added for the race fix or concurrent-access behavior
findings.body: The PR fixes a data race on entryPointAssetsCache but does not add any test (e.g., a test run with -race exercising concurrent calls to GetWebAssets) to verify the race is actually fixed or to guard against regressions. Without such a test, a future refactor could reintroduce the race undetected by CI.
